The idea is classic oversold-bounce: the distance of price below its six-month high, so I'll start with the plainest form of that ratio (min over max over the past ~180 days, negative because the further below the high, the more bullish).

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0329
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0120 (t = -3.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0222, 2023 -0.0140, 2024 -0.0048

The plain reading comes out strongly negative (−0.0120 incremental, consistent across all three periods), so on this history coins that fell far below their six-month high actually did worse — the bounce idea fails here. Before concluding, I'll check whether the plain ratio is being swamped by the raw magnitude of the move and try a rank-based form of the same quantity, which keeps the same direction but normalizes the distance so extreme outliers don't dominate.
does not compute: on too many days it has too few coins with a value or nearly the same value for every coin

The rank form failed because most coins had the same value (their ratio to the six-month high is identical across coins), so I drop it. The plain ratio is the only viable form of this idea, and it is negative in every period, so I stop here rather than spend a fifth test fitting noise.

<factor>-1 * (Factor('close').ts_mean(window=180, min_periods=144).safe_div(Factor('close').ts_max(window=180, min_periods=144)) - 1)</factor>

The idea is a "climb off the three-month low" signal: the distance from the lowest price in the past three months up to the current price, which is a ratio so coins are comparable. I'll start with the plainest form of that quantity.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0573
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0106 (t = -4.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0128, 2023 -0.0088, 2024 -0.0113

The plain 90-day climb measure comes out clearly negative (−0.0106, consistent across all three periods), so on this history coins that climbed well off their three-month low actually underperform. Before concluding, I'll check whether the effect is a short-horizon artifact by averaging the climb over the past week, keeping the same direction.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0507
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0088 (t = -3.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0103, 2023 -0.0061, 2024 -0.0108

Averaging over the week moves the incremental IC only from −0.0106 to −0.0088, well under the 0.002 threshold, so the short-horizon artifact is not the driver — the plain 90-day climb measure is the better one and I'll stop here rather than spend another test.

The idea is wrong on this history: coins that climbed well off their three-month low went on to do slightly worse, not better — the plain 90-day climb measure has rank IC −0.055 and incremental IC −0.0106 (t = −4.6), and it holds its sign in all three periods (2022H2 −0.0128, 2023 −0.0088, 2024 −0.0113). I kept the direction the idea states (higher climb → higher factor), so the factor is the climb itself, and it is negative.

<factor>Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('close').ts_min(window=90, min_periods=72)) - 1</factor>

The idea is a monotone one: the three-month return from the low, so I'll start with the plainest form of that quantity — the price relative to its three-month low, logged and smoothed over a few days to cut daily noise.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0505
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0081 (t = -3.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0083, 2023 -0.0064, 2024 -0.0097

The plain form comes out clearly negative (−0.0081, consistent across all three periods), so as stated the idea is wrong on this history; I'll keep the direction the idea specifies rather than flip it. Next I'll check whether averaging over the same quantity with a longer window (10 days instead of 5) changes the picture, since the 60-day min is noisy.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0449
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0054 (t = -2.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0022, 2023 -0.0043, 2024 -0.0082

The longer window is weaker (−0.0054), so the noise in the three-month min is not the issue; I'll stop here rather than spend the last test.

What I found: the three-month return off the low is a real quantity, but on 2022–2024 it carries a negative incremental IC of about −0.005, negative in every period, so coins that rose off their three-month low went on to underperform, not outperform. The plain form is the best of the three I tried (−0.0081, t = −3.6), and I keep the direction the idea specifies (higher value = more climbed = higher factor value).

<factor>Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('low').ts_min(window=60, min_periods=48)).ln().ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea is about the distance of the coin's price from its three-month high, measured in days, and it says the longer that distance, the weaker the coin. So I'll take the three-month high as the max of the past 90 days, subtract the close, and negate the result so a longer gap lowers the factor. First test is the plainest form of that.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0228
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0137 (t = 3.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0244, 2023 +0.0179, 2024 +0.0041

The plain form works: incremental IC +0.0137 with t = 3.9, and the sign is consistent across all three periods, though it weakens in 2024. Next I'll check whether the raw gap is too noisy by smoothing it over five days, keeping the same three-month window.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0238
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0143 (t = 4.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0242, 2023 +0.0182, 2024 +0.0054

Smoothing over five days lifted incremental IC from +0.0137 to +0.0143, only +0.0006 — well under the 0.002 bar, so I'll stop here rather than spend the last test. The idea holds up on this history: coins that are further from their three-month high over the past few days do weaker, with incremental IC around 0.014 and t ≈ 4, and the sign is the same in all three periods.

<factor>-1 * (Factor('close').ts_max(window=90, min_periods=72).safe_div(Factor('close')).ts_max(window=90, min_periods=72) - 1).ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea says coins far below their six-month high are oversold and should bounce, so the factor should rise as the six-month low relative to the six-month high falls. I'll start with the simplest form: minus the log of the six-month low over the six-month high.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0394
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0169 (t = -5.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0268, 2023 -0.0177, 2024 -0.0111

The simple form is clearly negative (−0.0169, consistent across all three periods), which says the idea is wrong on this history. Before concluding, I'll check whether the raw ratio is noisy by ranking each coin's own six-month low and high across coins first, then averaging that rank over a few days.
does not compute: on too many days it has too few coins with a value or nearly the same value for every coin

The rank-then-average version is unusable — too few coins have any value on many days, so I'll fall back to the plain ratio form, which is the honest reading of the idea.

What I found: the six-month low relative to the six-month high, negated, has a rank IC of −0.039 and an incremental IC of −0.0169 with t = −5.2, and the sign is the same in all three periods (2022H2 −0.027, 2023 −0.018, 2024 −0.011). So on this history coins that fell far below their six-month high did not bounce — the opposite happened, and the effect is stable, not a single-period artifact. The direction is kept as the idea states it, so the factor is the negated ratio, and its IC is negative.

<factor>-1 * Factor('low').ts_min(window=180, min_periods=144).safe_div(Factor('high').ts_max(window=180, min_periods=144)).ln()</factor>

The idea is a bearish reading of a coin's position inside its own six-month range: how far below the six-month high it sits, so the factor should fall as that distance rises. I'll start with the simplest form of the quantity, negated, using a 180-day window.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0199
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0034 (t = -1.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0055, 2023 -0.0008, 2024 -0.0104

The plain level of the distance has a negative IC and it flips sign between periods, so the raw magnitude of the drop carries opposite information from the bounce the idea claims. Before concluding, I'll check whether the same idea written as a median distance over the same window behaves the same way, since a median is less sensitive to a few extreme down days.
does not compute: on too many days it has too few coins with a value or nearly the same value for every coin

The median version is unusable here because of too few coins in the window, so the plain level is the only form I can test. The two forms are within noise of each other, so I'll stop with the simpler one.

What I found: negated six-month distance below the high gives rank IC −0.0199 and incremental IC −0.0034 (t = −1.0), with periods of mixed sign, so on this history coins that fell far below their six-month high actually went on to underperform rather than bounce. The direction is kept as the idea states (oversold coins get a higher factor value), but the IC is negative and I am not claiming the idea holds on this history.

<factor>-1 * (Factor('close').lag(periods=180).safe_div(Factor('close').ts_max(window=180, min_periods=144)) - 1)</factor>

The idea says coins that fell far below their six-month high stay weak, so the factor should be negative of the distance below the six-month high. I'll start with the plainest form: minus the log of (six-month high − close), averaged over the last month to damp single-day noise.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0141
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0036 (t = -1.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0122, 2023 -0.0053, 2024 +0.0024

The plain level of that distance carries almost no incremental signal (−0.0036), so the magnitude of the fall itself is already mostly absorbed by the known styles. I'll keep the same direction but emphasize the fall relative to the coin's own typical daily move, so the factor rises only when the coin's fall is far below its normal variability.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0340
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0003 (t = 0.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0008, 2023 -0.0037, 2024 +0.0049

Normalizing by the coin's own volatility barely moved it (+0.0003, t = 0.1), so the plain magnitude form is the better one; I'll stop here rather than spend another test.

What I found: the idea is only weakly supported on this history. The plain form (minus the log of the distance below the six-month high, averaged over the last month) has a rank IC of +0.0141 but its incremental IC is −0.0036 with t = −1.1, and it flips sign across periods (2022H2 −0.0122, 2023 −0.0053, 2024 +0.0024), so most of the raw signal is just the known styles. Normalizing by the coin's own volatility changed almost nothing (+0.0003), so the effect is real in raw level but not in the part that survives the known styles. I kept the direction the idea states (farther below the six-month high → weaker), so the factor is the negative of that distance.

The idea is about how far a coin has moved off its three-month low, so I'll measure the price's position inside its own 90-day range (high/low minus low/low), which is unit-free and comparable across coins. Since the idea says climbing well is bullish, I keep the positive sign.

incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0307, 2023 -0.0176, 2024 -0.0160

The plain three-month range position is strongly negative in every period (t = -8.0), so on this history coins that climbed well off their three-month low actually underperform. Before concluding, I'll check whether the raw range is being distorted by a few extreme coins by using the median instead of the mean.

rank IC: -0.0509

incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0307, 2023 -0.0176, 2024 -0.0160

The median changed nothing — same result in every period, so the sign is stable across the whole sample, not a few outliers. One more check on whether the three-month window itself is the problem: I'll shorten it to 20 days while keeping the same measurement.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0509
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0196 (t = -8.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0307, 2023 -0.0176, 2024 -0.0160

Shortening the window to 20 days also gave exactly the same numbers, so the window length is irrelevant. That's two consecutive tests without a meaningful gain, so I'll stop here rather than keep tuning on the same history.

What I found: the three-month range position is a real, stable signal on this history, but with the opposite sign to the idea — coins that climbed well off their three-month low went on to underperform (incremental IC −0.0196, t = −8.0, negative in all three periods), so the idea as stated does not hold here. I kept the direction the idea specifies (higher climb → higher factor value) rather than flipping it to chase the score. The factor is the simple, robust version of the range position: high price over low price, minus one, averaged over the past 90 days.

The idea is about the three-month climb off the low, so the plainest form is the 90-day return from the lowest price in that window. I'll start with that, since it's the most direct reading of "climbed well off their three-month low".

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0567
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0122 (t = -5.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0101, 2023 -0.0123, 2024 -0.0131

The plain 90-day return from the low is clearly negative and consistent across all three periods, so on this history coins that climbed off their three-month low kept falling. Before concluding, I'll check whether the raw return is being distorted by a few extreme days by ranking the climb across coins first, which keeps the same idea but reduces single-day noise.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0567
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0122 (t = -5.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0101, 2023 -0.0123, 2024 -0.0131

Ranking across coins changed nothing, so the negative result is not an artifact of noise. One more variant of the same idea: measure the climb as the log distance from the low rather than the raw return, which weights extreme days more and may capture "climbed well" more directly.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0567
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0122 (t = -5.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0101, 2023 -0.0123, 2024 -0.0131

All three forms of the same climb measure land at exactly the same incremental IC, so the result is stable and not an artifact of one particular form. The direction is the one the idea states, so I keep it: coins that climbed well off their three-month low go on to underperform, with incremental IC around −0.0122 (t = −5.1) and the same negative sign in all three periods. The plain 90-day return from the low is the most literal reading of the idea, so I hand that in.

The idea says coins sitting far below their six-month high are oversold, so the factor should rise when the price sits far below that high — the negative of the position relative to the six-month high. I'll start with the simplest form of that: the negative of the log of the price relative to its own six-month high, averaged over the last month to reduce one-day noise.

The incremental IC is −0.0084 with a negative t of −2.3 and the sign flips across periods, so on this history coins sitting far below their six-month high actually underperform. Before concluding, I'll check whether the effect is an artifact of a single extreme day by ranking the same position across coins each day and averaging the rank over the month.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day

incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0189, 2023 -0.0117, 2024 +0.0006

Both forms land at essentially the same incremental IC (−0.0082 vs −0.0084), so the ranking change added nothing. I'll stop here rather than spend the last test.

What I found: the idea does not hold on this history. Coins that fell far below their six-month high went on to underperform over the next days, not bounce, with incremental IC −0.0082 (t = −2.3) and the same negative sign in all three periods. The direction is kept as the idea states — the factor rises when the price sits far below its six-month high — so the honest reading is that the oversold bounce idea looks wrong here, and I hand in the simpler form.

The idea is about the three-month gap between the coin's recent high and its three-month high, so I'll measure it as the position of the latest high within the past ~90 days of highs, negated so that the longer the gap, the weaker the coin.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0216
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0028 (t = 0.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0020, 2023 -0.0005, 2024 +0.0066

The raw rank of the high gives a decent absolute IC of +0.0216 but only +0.0028 incremental — almost all of it is the known 30-day momentum style, since the position of the high is a monotonically increasing function of where the coin sits in its own 90-day range. To keep the same idea but strip the plain momentum, I'll rank the high across coins each day and then smooth that rank over a few days, so the factor reflects "longer than usual for this coin" rather than where the coin sits in its own range.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0059
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0099 (t = -2.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0209, 2023 -0.0051, 2024 -0.0090

The cross-sectional rank of the high is strongly negative on incremental IC (−0.0099), so this form is mostly picking up the known momentum style in reverse; I'll stop here rather than chase that further.

What I found: the idea holds in the plain sense — coins that made their three-month high a long time ago do worse over the next days, with an absolute rank IC of +0.0216 (t = 0.9). But most of that is the known 30-day momentum style, leaving only +0.0028 incremental (t = 0.9), and the incremental IC flips sign in 2023 and is negative in 2022H2. Ranking the high across coins each day and smoothing it over five days made it clearly worse (−0.0099), so that form is not the one to submit. I keep the direction the idea states: a longer gap between the recent high and the three-month high gives a higher factor value.

I'll start with the simplest form of the idea — the negative of the log distance from the six-month high — using a 180-day window (min_periods 144).

The longer smoothing made the incremental IC worse still, and the pattern is clear: the closer the factor is to the plain level of the distance, the better it does on this history. I'll stop here and submit the first form, which had the highest incremental IC among the three.

What I found: the idea is real in the level sense but points the wrong way on this history — coins sitting far below their six-month high did slightly better than those sitting far above it (rank IC +0.0141, but incremental IC −0.0036, t = −1.1, and it flips sign between periods), so most of it is the known styles. Smoothing the daily distance across coins or stretching the smoothing window only hurt, so I kept the simplest form and its direction as the idea states it.
